title: Does what it's supposed to, just be careful.
text:
Does what it's supposed to, just be careful.. I purchased this 1-gallon water distiller for producing water for my carnivorous plants (they are sensitive to contaminants.) It produces distilled water as it should, but I have a few gripes.
First, and most importantly, the unit's design is two pieces. A top containing the fan lifts off, and the bottom contains the water chamber and heating elements. The top piece has its own plug which must be plugged into the base. Then, the base has its own plug, which is removable and plugs into the outlet.
If you are not careful, there is a *serious* risk of electrocution and/or damaging the unit due to this design. The plug on the base of the unit is pretty much guaranteed to be exposed to water dripping down the sides when you remove the lid to add more water. I highly recommend covering the back side of the unit with a dry towel when you remove the top. Water that has evaporated in the machine will still be present in the top and will drip all over the place.
Additionally, when you go to fill up the tank, ensure you don't allow any water to drip over the side of the base. (The water tank is not removable from the base, you have to tote the whole thing to the sink or bring a pitcher of water to the machine.)
Despite the flaws in its design and a lingering suspicion that cleaning this thing will be difficult, I would still recommend it for those who need distilled water on demand. It saves you so much trouble buying and lugging it from the store. Just use caution!
